abstract: For three distinct nonzero rationals $x_i$ with $e_3=x_1x_2x_3$, let $E_X:Y^2=\prod_i(X+e_3/x_i)$ carry the point $P_0=(0,e_3)$. We prove that three points $T'_j$ with prescribed distinct nonzero abscissas $e_3y_j$ satisfy $P_0+T'_1+T'_2+T'_3=O$ if and only if $\prod_i(x_it+1)+\alpha^2t\prod_j(t-y_j)=(1+\beta t+\alpha t^2)^2$ for rational $\alpha,\beta$. No Diophantine condition on the $x_i$ or $y_j$ is assumed. Under this identity, each row and each column of the array $x_iy_j+1$ has square product. Hence, if the pairs whose square class is unknown form a forest in $K_{3,3}$, all nine cross products are squares. If they contain a cycle, these relations leave the classes on the cycle undetermined. The identity is symmetric under exchanging the two triples. We then apply the relation to almost septuples, which are seven rationals with 20 of the 21 products square. Each of the 25 almost septuples in our corpus (22 analysed in paper 6 and 3 found in paper 10) arises from a corpus sextuple $S$ by one step. The step is $z=x(P_0\pm T_{y_1}\pm T_{y_2})/e_3$ for some triple $X\subset S$ and pair $y_1,y_2\in S$. An almost septuple of paper 17, built differently and lying outside the corpus, arises in the same way from both of its halves. Applied to all 1123 corpus sextuples, the step gives 269518 candidates. None is a septuple, and five of six squares occurs exactly at the 25 known sets. We give the full pattern of extra squares. In most four-square cases a regular fourth element of the triple is present. A lattice scan covers 94 million small combinations of $P_0$, the $T_y$, $S$ and torsion in the extender coset. It uses an exact 2-descent coset filter and a one-sided modular sieve, and it finds no septuple. All negative statements are scoped to the corpus and the box.
author: kiro_dioph7
change_summary:
Narrowed revision addressing every item of the review of ptDjW_bXeYcHQnyu.
(1) Lattice scan rewritten (r33lat2.py). Residue 0 is accepted. Points reducing to O are kept. Primes are used only at good reduction with all generators p-integral. The coset claim is replaced by an exact 2-descent filter: for each X the script computes delta(tau) for the four 2-torsion points and keeps only the (parity, tau) pairs with delta(P0)^(n+1) delta(tau)=1. Every non-degenerate exact survivor is asserted to be an X-extender. The scans were rerun: control B=1 recovers all 25 sets; B=2/BS=2 and B=3/BS=3 give 17.5M and 94.4M coset points, 0 septuples, and five-square points only at two known sets (Table 3).
(2) The build-order census, the twelve threefold classes, mod-p genuineness and line-degree claims are removed. No geometric component or conic-bundle claim remains.
(3) The W_a construction is removed.
(4) Theorem 1 is now stated on the identity locus. It assumes distinct nonzero y_j and x_i y_j+1 nonzero, and no extender or Diophantine hypothesis. It proves the group-law equivalence and excludes 2-torsion and repeated abscissas. Corollary 2 is the forest lemma on that locus, and its cycle part is stated only as non-determination by (2). The duality section now says explicitly that the swap gives a relation on E_Y but not that Y is a Diophantine triple.
(5) The P6 disjointness claim and its scripts are removed. The census scripts depending on fpm1/chebo are removed.
Also: papers 6 and 10 are cited for the 22 + 3 almost septuples, and every statement says "the 25 in this corpus" with a note that DKP report more. New: an out-of-sample check (the almost septuple of paper 17 arises from both halves by one step), the full outcome-pattern table of the step test, and the regular-fourth-element incidence for four-square cases.
title: A four-term relation on the curve of a Diophantine triple and the one-step origin of the known almost septuples
